input.strategy_title: GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Platform teams fund shared GPU clusters but cannot attribute consumption to the
projects using them, so capacity costs are socialized and heavy users have no
incentive to release resources. The in-flight metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is delivering per-project GPU-hour usage data; this strategy
builds the administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of that data. The
metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until that
strategy lands — reporting work here consumes it, and must not re-implement
collection.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API for finance tooling. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- The metering collection pipeline itself (RHAISTRAT-9990)
- Currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars

## Open Questions

1. The metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report
   implementation consuming it carries that external timing risk.

# Expose per-project Kueue GPU quota data for administrator consumption reporting

## Description

This epic delivers a consumable, per-project view of Kueue GPU quota and
current quota usage in the Distributed Workloads component, so that
administrator-facing chargeback reporting can compare each project's GPU-hour
consumption against its Kueue quota. Today the platform's Kueue metrics
expose pending/admitted workload counts per queue, which is not sufficient
for per-project GPU quota comparison; this epic provides that data surface.

## Scope

- Expose, per project (namespace), the project's Kueue GPU quota and current
  quota usage, derived from the platform's Kueue quota model
  (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue semantics).
- Choose and implement the exposure surface (metrics, custom resource, or
  API) — an implementation decision for the Distributed Workloads team; the
  strategy does not prescribe one.
- Document the exposed data contract (shape and semantics of the per-project
  quota information) for consuming teams.
- Ensure projects without a Kueue quota are represented predictably
  (reportable as no-quota) rather than omitted silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- For every project that has a Kueue GPU quota, the project's GPU quota and
  current quota usage are retrievable through the exposed surface.
- The exposed quota information is consistent with the platform's Kueue
  quota model (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue semantics), verified against the
  deployed Kueue configuration.
- The data contract of the exposed surface is documented.
- Existing Kueue queueing and admission behavior is unchanged (regression
  check on the queueing path).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1) — enables the quota side of "current-month consumption against
  each project's Kueue quota" in the administrator view.

# Administrator GPU-hour consumption reports with CSV export and reporting API

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator-facing per-project GPU-hour consumption
reporting in the Dashboard: reports of per-project GPU-hour usage over
selectable time ranges, computed from the per-project GPU-hour usage data
delivered by the GPU usage metering work (RHAISTRAT-9990). It also delivers
the export and retrieval access modes of the same reports — CSV export and a
stable API for finance tooling. Collection of usage data is owned by the
metering strategy and is not re-implemented here.

## Scope

- Administrator report view in the Dashboard: per-project GPU-hour
  consumption over administrator-selectable time ranges.
- Report computation consumes the metering data as delivered by the GPU
  usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990); no re-implementation of usage
  collection.
- CSV export of the displayed report (same project/time-range data).
- Stable retrieval API over the same report data, suitable for finance
  tooling integration.
- Administrator-only access to the reports, export, and API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can view per-project GPU-hour consumption for a
  selectable time range, computed from the delivered metering data.
- The report for a given project and time range can be exported as CSV and
  opens correctly in spreadsheet tooling.
- The same report data is retrievable through a stable API usable by
  finance tooling.
- Report access (view, export, API) is restricted to platform
  administrators.
- Report computation conforms to the metering data schema as finalized by
  the GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990); schema finalization
  changes are absorbed in the consumption layer and the reports re-validate
  cleanly against the finalized schema.

## Risks / Notes

- The metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until
  that strategy lands; this epic carries that external timing risk. Reports
  are implemented and validated against the metering data as currently
  delivered and re-validated at finalization (fix-and-adapt).
- The Dashboard architecture (no data plane; Kubernetes API only) does not
  currently define a surface for non-CR time-series data or an external
  report API; the consumption path and API surface must align with what the
  metering strategy delivers. Flagged in the decomposition health warnings —
  not an acceptance criterion on this epic's deliverable.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption
  reports over selectable time ranges.
- HLR-2 (P1, bundled) — CSV export and stable API retrieval are access modes
  of the same report surface built for HLR-1; they share the report data
  structure and are not separately schedulable, so they are kept in this
  epic rather than split out.

# Administrator view of current-month consumption against Kueue quota

## Description

This epic delivers the Dashboard administrator view showing each project's
current-month GPU-hour consumption alongside that project's Kueue GPU quota,
so administrators can see how much of each project's quota has been consumed
this month. It consumes two existing capabilities rather than re-implementing
them: the per-project consumption reporting delivered for chargeback
reporting, and the per-project Kueue GPU quota data exposed by the
Distributed Workloads component.

## Scope

- Administrator view in the Dashboard listing projects with their
  current-month GPU-hour consumption and their Kueue GPU quota, presented as
  a consumption-vs-quota comparison.
- Reuse of the per-project report capability for the current-month
  consumption figures (current month is a fixed time range of the same
  report data) — no independent consumption-data retrieval.
- Reuse of the per-project quota data surface exposed by the Distributed
  Workloads component for the quota figures — no independent quota
  computation.
- Administrator-only access.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The administrator view shows, per project, current-month GPU-hour
  consumption alongside the project's Kueue GPU quota.
- Consumption figures come from the chargeback reporting capability and
  quota figures from the exposed per-project quota data; neither is
  re-implemented in this epic.
- Projects without a Kueue quota are shown as no-quota in the view, per the
  documented data contract of the exposed per-project quota surface, rather
  than silently omitted.
- View access is restricted to platform administrators.
- The view's current-month consumption figures, obtained through the
  per-project report capability, re-validate cleanly against the metering
  data schema as finalized by the GPU usage metering strategy
  (RHAISTRAT-9990); schema finalization changes are absorbed upstream in
  the report consumption layer, not re-implemented in this view.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1) — the Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption
  against each project's Kueue quota.

# Documentation of chargeback report semantics and export integration

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator and finance-tooling documentation for
GPU chargeback reporting: what the reports mean (in particular what counts as
a GPU-hour and how per-project attribution works) and how to integrate with
the report export (CSV) and retrieval API. It documents the capability as
built, so it runs after the implementation work.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Report semantics: what counts as a GPU-hour, how per-project attribution
  is derived from the metering data, and how selectable time ranges affect
  the reported figures.
- Reading the consumption-vs-quota administrator view: what the quota
  comparison shows and how to interpret projects without a quota.
- Export integration for finance tooling: retrieving reports via the stable
  API and consuming the CSV export.
- Access prerequisites for administrators (permissions required to view
  reports).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers report semantics, including a clear definition of
  what counts as a GPU-hour, consistent with the semantics finalized by the
  GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990).
- Documentation covers export integration (CSV export and API retrieval) for
  finance tooling.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reporting
  capability by the implementing team before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2) — documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a
  GPU-hour) and export integration.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9018 (GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators)

Strategy status: Refinement Done. Strategy priority: Major.

## Strategy Parsing Notes

The strategy is deliberately sparse. The following required sections are
missing or degenerate (health warnings recorded below):

- **Affected Components** lists component names only — no "what changes" and
  no owner team per component. Scopes and teams were inferred (see Health
  Warnings).
- **Impacted Teams table**: absent. Teams inferred from
  `.context/architecture-context/` owning teams (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard;
  Distributed Workloads → Distributed Workloads).
- **Dependencies table**: absent. The only dependency is the frontmatter
  `depends-on: RHAISTRAT-9990` link and the Open Questions entry.
- **Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)**: absent. Epic ACs were derived
  from the HLRs.
- **Non-Functional Requirements**: absent.
- **Staff Engineer Input**: absent — no overrides to apply.

## Step 0 Triage

Not below threshold: the strategy affects two components (Dashboard,
Distributed Workloads) owned by two teams, and the reporting work carries an
unresolved external data-contract dependency, so ≥67% High AI implementability
does not hold. Not documentation-only: HLR-1..3 require code changes. Full
decomposition follows.

## Open Question Evaluation (Step 3)

The strategy's single open question — the metering data schema finalizes only
when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands — was evaluated against the Step 3 decision rule
("does the answer change which downstream epics exist or what they do?"):

- **Which epics exist**: unchanged. The reporting view, export/API, quota
  comparison view, and documentation epics exist regardless of the schema's
  final shape.
- **What they do**: unchanged at the functional level. The schema shape is a
  consumption-layer detail of the reporting implementation; resolution
  requires no technical work by these teams — the answer arrives when the
  sibling strategy lands. Failure mode is fix-and-adapt (adjust the
  consumption layer), i.e. an acceptance-criterion gate, not an
  investigation.
- The dependency is a sibling **internal strategy** that resolves itself
  (analogous to Rule 21's "third party resolves" case): modeled as a
  **precondition with tiered delivery** (see Tiered Delivery), with no epic
  invented for RHAISTRAT-9990 and no DAG edge to it (there is no epic to edge
  to).

Conclusion: **no Investigation epic**. The risk is carried as ACs plus
Risks/Notes on the consuming epics and as a health warning below.

|----|-------|------|------|-----------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E001 | Expose per-project Kueue GPU quota data for administrator consumption reporting | Implementation | Distributed Workloads | Distributed Workloads | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E002 | Administrator GPU-hour consumption reports with CSV export and reporting API | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E003 | Administrator view of current-month consumption against Kueue quota | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E004 | Documentation of chargeback report semantics and export integration | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Dashboard | Documentation | P1 |

Priorities: E002 carries HLR-1 (P0). E001 and E003 carry HLR-3 (P1). E004 is a
`docs-authoring` epic — exempt from priority inheritance; its priority is
derived from the strategy frontmatter `priority: Major` → P1 (HLR-4 is P2 in
the HLR table, but the docs-authoring priority exception governs the epic).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 — per-project Kueue GPU quota data (DW)"] --> E003["E003 — consumption vs quota admin view"]
    E002["E002 — consumption reports + CSV/API (Dashboard)"] --> E003
    E001 --> E004["E004 — report semantics & export docs"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

Critical path: E001 → E003 → E004 (and E002 → E003 → E004), length 3.

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (build-against artifact) | The quota-comparison view's code builds against the per-project quota surface E001 exposes (an API/CR/metrics surface, not a configuration reference). |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 12/13 + shared-surface rule | The quota view displays current-month consumption, which is the report capability over a fixed time range; the edge prevents two epics building the same consumption-data surface independently. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes what was built, including the quota data semantics. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation covers report semantics and export integration. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation covers the consumption-vs-quota view. |

Non-edges, deliberately:

- **No E001 → E002 edge**: the P0 reporting work does not consume the quota

  work (priority-inversion guard).
- **No edge to/from RHAISTRAT-9990**: it is another strategy, not an epic in
  this DAG. Its schema finality is expressed as ACs (conformance gate) and
  Risks on E002/E003, per the Rule 21 "third party resolves" pattern plus

- **No Investigation epic**: see Open Question Evaluation above.

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): Affected Components has no
   per-component change descriptions or owners; Impacted Teams table,
   Dependencies table, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and NFRs are
   absent. Epic scopes, teams, and ACs were derived from the HLRs and the
   architecture-context owning teams. Human verification of the inferred
   scopes is recommended at review.
2. **External dependency timing risk** (the strategy's open question): the
   metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until
   that strategy lands. No epic is invented for it (it resolves itself);
   conformance is an AC gate on E002/E003 and the semantics risk is noted on
   E004. Timing is outside this strategy's control — a schedule risk, not an
   acceptance criterion.
3. **Architecture tension on the reporting data path** (scope trap): the
   Dashboard architecture context states the Dashboard "owns no data plane"
   and its interfaces are "Kubernetes API only; no private component APIs".
   HLR-1/HLR-2 require computing reports from non-CR metering data and
   exposing a stable API for finance tooling. The strategy does not specify
   the consumption/access surface; the decomposition keeps this at functional
   level (consume the metering delivery as provided by RHAISTRAT-9990) and
   flags the ungrounded API surface rather than inventing one.
4. **Inferred Distributed Workloads scope**: the strategy lists Distributed
   Workloads as affected but describes no change for it. HLR-3's
   per-project Kueue quota comparison is the only DW-adjacent requirement,
   and current Kueue metrics (pending/admitted workloads per queue) do not
   expose per-project GPU quota usage, so E001 scopes that exposure. If
   review determines the Dashboard can read sufficient quota data directly
   from existing Kueue CRs, E001 reduces to a validation acceptance
   criterion on E003.
5. **Inferred docs team**: no Impacted Teams table exists; E004 is assigned
   to the RHOAI Dashboard team as the primary delivering team for the
   documented capability.
6. **Priority inversions**: none found. E002 (P0) blocks no P0-lower work;
   E001/E003 (P1) do not gate any P0 epic.

## Tiered Delivery

External dependency with uncertain timing: the metering data schema owned by
RHAISTRAT-9990 (in flight). Can the strategy deliver partial value without
the final schema? **Yes** — the metering data is already being delivered by
the in-flight strategy, so:

- **Tier 1 (independent work, starts now)**: E001 (fully independent of
  metering data — quota side only), E002 and E003 implemented and validated
  against the metering data as currently delivered.
- **Tier 2 (dependency-gated)**: final-schema conformance — once RHAISTRAT-9990
  lands, the reporting output is re-validated against the finalized schema
  and the documentation reflects the final report semantics. This gate is
  expressed as acceptance criteria on E002/E003 (and a semantics AC on E004),
  not as separate epics. Fallback if the final schema diverges: adapt the
  reporting consumption layer (fix-and-retry); the reporting surfaces and
  quota work are unaffected.
